external_entities.name: Customer
external_entities.description: Customers who browse and place sock orders through the mobile app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

external_entities.name: Marketing
external_entities.description: The marketing staff who maintain the catalogue.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application through which customers browse and order.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: Web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app, which stores customer information and hands orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: Fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that sends dispatch confirmations by fax to the number stored against the order.
processes.source_excerpt: The gateway dials the number stored against the order
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: Macros
processes.description: Spreadsheet macros that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
processes.notes: The spreadsheet macros were described as a stopgap and are still present.

data_stores.name: User database
data_stores.description: The database holding customer names, addresses, and payment card details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: Flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file containing delivery addresses written by SIMS.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: Spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue, including prices and product copy, with macros that update the web API.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_stores.name: Marketing laptop
data_stores.description: The office laptop where the marketing spreadsheet lives.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: app requests
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS, it's on the list.
data_flows.notes: The source explicitly says the connection is HTTP, not HTTPS.

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and payment card

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: confirmation with customer name and address

data_flows.name: keep catalogue
data_flows.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: Office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop and spreadsheet are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is internet-facing because customers use the mobile app to order from Sokify online.
assumptions.basis: The description says Sokify sells socks online and that the customer mobile app talks to the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly identifies it as a mobile app rather than a website.

assumptions.assumption: The macros present a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: They are spreadsheet macros running in a spreadsheet, not a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment card details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the user database contains customer name, address, and the card they paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The source states that only delivery addresses are stored in the flat file.
